newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Feb electricity demand up 2.2 pct year/year.
newsitem.headline: Japan Feb electricity demand up 2.2 pct year/year.

text.p: Demand for electricity supplied by Japan's nine major power utilities in February rose 2.2 percent from the same month a year earlier to 66.8 billion kilowatt hours (kWh), the Federation of Electric Power Companies said on Wednesday.
Household electricity demand in February grew by 4.0 percent to about 22.0 billion kWh, while commercial electricity demand rose by 3.8 percent to 13.3 billion kWh.

Electricity demand for heating declined because of milder-than-average weather from the end of January to early February. However, household demand climbed during this period because of some extra days in meter inspection schedules for some households, a federation spokesman said.
The increase in demand for commercial electricity was attributed to a firm growth in contracts.
Large-lot industrial electricity demand in February fell 0.4 percent from 1996, which was a leap year, to 20.8 billion kWh. It was the first year-on-year drop in six months.
